newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon reports third Ebola death in capital.
newsitem.headline: Gabon reports third Ebola death in capital.

text.p: A third person has died in Gabon's capital Libreville after being infected by the deadly Ebola virus, medical officials said on Saturday.
The victim, who died in Melen hospital on the outskirts of the city this week, was a child understood to be the brother of an earlier victim, one medical source said.
Ebola, which can kill up to eight out of 10 people it infects, causes fever and uncontrollable bleeding. It is transmitted through contact with contaminated body fluids.

Medical officials trace the victims in the capital to an upcountry outbreak but residents are growing anxious about the reports of the presence in the city of the virus, which usually surfaces away from large population areas.
Growing numbers have stopped offering kisses on the cheek or handshakes -- traditional greetings in the Central African former French colony and throughout Francophone Africa.
The head of the committee coordinating the fight against the virus told state radio on Friday every precaution was being taken to isolate anyone who had had contact with victims.
"Those who have been in contact are under surveillance for 42 days, that is twice the critical period," Doctor Medard Toung Mve said. Medical sources say about 30 people are quarantined.
Gabon has reported three Ebola epidemics in the past year but earlier cases were in remote forest areas.
The first victim in Libreville, a man, died on December 18. Health officials traced the latest outbreak to people who came into contact with Ebola dead in north east Gabon in October.
Ebola killed seven people in Oogue-Ivindo province there in October after 13 died there in February. It killed 245 people in and around the Zairean town of Kikwit in 1995.
